links.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity and added testing after software version update, with and without threshold recalibration
links.effect: At the old cut-off 0.217, new version had sensitivity 96.4% but specificity 23.1% (p<0.001), +36.4% Ultra testing; recalibrated to 0.480, specificity 43.2%, +4.1% testing, p=0.148.
links.quote: When a second cut-off threshold is selected for the newer v3.9.0.1 software so that it achieves a 90% sensitivity (0.480), there is no statistical difference with the newer software’s specificity (43.2%) or the additional Ultra tests indicated (+4.1%) compared with the v3.1.0.0 software version (p = 0.148) at its original threshold.

links.outcome: Effect of recalibrating decision threshold after model update on specificity and testing volume
links.effect: Without recalibration new version specificity fell to 23.1% (+36.4% testing); after recalibration to 0.480, specificity 43.2% and +4.1% testing, not significantly different from old version.
links.quote: When using an cut-off threshold optimized for the older software version, the newer software was significantly less accurate than its predecessors.

links.outcome: Sensitivity/specificity of new software at original versus re-calibrated cut-off threshold
links.effect: Original threshold: specificity 23.1% vs 45.8% for old version; re-calibrated threshold 0.480 gave 90.4% sensitivity and 43.2% specificity, no significant difference (p=0.148).
links.quote: However, when the cut-off threshold was re-calibrated, there were no significant differences in sensitivity and specificity between the software versions.

links.outcome: Performance of updated software version at previously validated threshold
links.effect: New version at old threshold: specificity 23.1% vs 45.8%, +36.4% diagnostic testing; performance matched predecessor only after recalibration.
links.quote: Between successive Lunit CAD software versions, there was a significant increase in the median abnormality score which translates to significantly decreased specificity and thus significantly increased diagnostic testing indication if the abnormality score cut-off threshold is not re-calibrated for the new software version.

links.outcome: Retesting after software update to confirm performance and thresholds remain valid
links.effect: Update raised AUC 0.76 to 0.78 (p=0.029) but shifted abnormality scores, cutting specificity at old threshold from 45.8% to 23.1%.
links.quote: As new CAD software versions are rolled out, cut-off thresholds must be re-calibrated to ensure the continued accuracy of CXR interpretation.

links.outcome: Performance after software update at unchanged cutoff
links.effect: At cutoff 0.217, v3.9.0.1 had sensitivity 96.4%, specificity 23.1%, and +36.4% Ultra testing versus v3.1.0.0 specificity 45.8%.
links.quote: Using this same cut-off threshold, the newer v3.9.0.1 software achieves a significantly higher sensitivity of 96.4%, but a significantly lower specificity of 23.1% (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity, and testing after threshold recalibration

links.outcome: AUC differences across demographic and clinical subgroups
links.effect: Newer software improved AUC in past TB 0.67 vs 0.73 (p=0.003), older individuals 0.75 vs 0.77 (p=0.040), and males 0.73 vs 0.76 (p=0.008).
